transcript.text: During my reconciliation work this week, I identified an important cost classification issue that affects the budget. Of the $4,000,000 total program cost, exactly $1,200,000 relates to configuring and testing new systems before they are ready for use. Under standard accounting treatment, this portion should be capitalized rather than expensed. The remaining $2,800,000 represents subscription and operating costs. I've recorded this split in my working model but haven't circulated it until now. This means the budget's P&L impact in year one would be $2,800,000 in operating expense, with $1,200,000 capitalized as an asset and amortized over the useful life of the system. Elena, this should factor into your budget approval and cash flow assumptions.

transcript.text: Thank you, Jonas. That's a helpful clarification on the cost classification. Now let me share what Internal Audit has identified. During my review this week, I found that the finance-transformation program will create production access to financial data through the new systems and processes being implemented. This is a significant control consideration. Based on this finding, I'm recommending that Elena's approval of the program must require two specific control conditions: first, dual authorization for any production access to financial data, and second, a quarterly user-access review to monitor and validate that access on an ongoing basis. I have these requirements documented in my draft finding, though I should note I have not yet formally added them to the project control checklist. Elena, I believe these access controls should be built directly into the program's execution conditions before sign-off, given the sensitivity of the financial data that will be accessible through the new systems.
